owner: HW-07 Comm-Core (co-sign SW-05 Collective/Comm-Compute, SW-01 Runtime)
scope: Every alternative HW-07 considers for the collective control path lives here. integration/detailed/comm_core_search.js enumerates the product of the searched dimensions, drops invalid combinations, scores the rest on the detailed protocol model and writes only the winner to out/detailed/comm_core_design.json. The per-option comparison is quoted in the document, section 7.
evidence: Cycle counts and areas are ASSUMPTIONs (O-018) at the die clock and the N4 reference process until RTL or a cycle model calibrates them; the MTIA figures are measured on a different chip and are order-of-magnitude references only.

floorplan.source: teams/hardware/docs/05_ON_DIE_NOC.md section 2 (x, y); control packets cost TECH.routerCycles per Manhattan hop
floorplan.dieDispatcher: OPEN: not placed; a leg to or from it is charged meshSide hops

requirements.evidence: ASSUMPTION: double-buffered graph so the next model's graph loads while the current one runs; at most half of the Comm Core busy per token; WQE size is R.MEM.wqeCqeBytes; one RV32 management core with 16 KiB I/D about 0.03 mm2; a firmware job on the critical path that shares its core with epoch and exception work waits up to 40 cycles
requirements.contractReason: the per-collective ceiling is the L1 budget contract's B-TAU max (integration/detailed/design_contract.js), not a local OPT constant: the comm domain answers for that entry

constraints: every collective class: protocol time + control path <= the contract's B-TAU ceiling, so the published point is unchanged; this also keeps the raw latency within the raw budget because TPS does not rise with tau
graph storage fits the local SRAM with graphBuffers copies when the graph is stored locally
Comm Core busy time per token <= maxUtilization x raw latency
objective: least AI Core time per token spent on communication control
largest spec-tau slack of the slowest class (margin for the O-018 cycle calibration)

placement.question: Where the Comm Core sits on the die mesh

spare32.evidence: spare east of the Reduce engine

spare23.evidence: spare south of the Reduce engine, centre of the mesh

spare33.evidence: spare diagonal to the Reduce engine

gateway.evidence: inside the UCIe/RDMA gateway tile GW2, next to the NIC

trigger.question: What starts a collective once its producers are done

counterCompare.evidence: hardware completion counters fed by the Core scoreboards over the Control NoC; compare with the patch-table threshold (MTIA 300 device-triggered collective, wait-on-value)

coreStore.evidence: the producer Core issues a posted store to the Comm Core after its last tile

firmwarePoll.evidence: the management RISC-V polls completion counters: a loop over up to 8 pending counters at 4 cycles each

dieDispatcher.evidence: completions go to the Die Dispatcher (08), which sends a start command to the Comm Core

wqeGeneration.question: Who produces the RDMA work requests (WQEs)

templatePatch.evidence: precompiled WQE templates in the collective graph, patched per epoch (MTIA 300 Message Engine graph)

descriptorExpand.evidence: an address generator expands one per-collective descriptor and a per-class peer table into WQEs

firmwareBuild.evidence: the management RISC-V builds each 128 B WQE (four 32 B stores plus field arithmetic), MTIA 300 CPU-M style

coreBuild.evidence: the producer AI Core posts the WQEs and rings the NIC itself (MTIA 300 PE, about 450 ns measured, HCCL arXiv 2608.00358)

controlProcessor.evidence: a control processor dispatches each collective (MTIA 300 CPU-C, 2.9 us measured, HCCL arXiv 2608.00358)

txLanes.question: How many WQE generation lanes run in parallel (one lane feeds all active NICs in turn)

doorbell.question: How a WQE reaches the NIC

directPush.evidence: WQE written with the doorbell into an on-NIC queue (MTIA Express Doorbell); needs a NIC-side WQE buffer

ringFetch.evidence: doorbell only; the NIC reads the WQE back from a ring in Comm Core SRAM, one round trip before the first WQE

commitCounting.question: Who counts the inbound commits of a mailbox slot and tells the consumer

hwCounters.evidence: CC-RX hardware commit counters per slot for two epochs; READY notify and reduce WQE on the last commit

firmwareCount.evidence: the management RISC-V handles each inbound commit (load, increment, compare, store)

consumerPoll.evidence: the consumer Core polls the slot flags in Shared SRAM, one round trip per poll

signal.question: How the commit signal of a one-sided put reaches the remote counter (memory semantics)

putWithSignal.evidence: the 16 B flag rides at the tail of the data packet and is applied as an atomic add after the data is visible: the protocol model as published

separateSignal.evidence: a second WQE per peer on the same ordered QP carries the flag: twice the NIC issue and one more header+flag packet per message

writeThenSignal.evidence: the flag is sent only after the data write is acknowledged (unordered fabric, no remote fence): one more round trip per message before the commit

graphStore.question: Where the collective graph (templates or descriptors) lives

localSram.evidence: Comm Core SRAM, no fetch on the critical path

sharedSram.evidence: nearest Shared SRAM slice; one mesh round trip per collective before the first WQE

mc.evidence: HBM/MC behind the gateway (MTIA 300 fetches the graph from HBM); ASSUMPTION 150 ns access

managementCores.question: Management RISC-V cores (graph load, epoch, timeout/poison/retry, and any firmware job on the critical path)

instances.reason: the simulator keeps one collective in flight per die and the chosen design is busy for a few percent of the token; one per package would add a die-to-die hop to every trigger

txRxEngines.chosen: separate TX and RX state machines
txRxEngines.reason: inbound commits must not queue behind WQE generation of the next collective

dataSemantics.chosen: memory semantics (one-sided put/get/atomic on global addresses)
dataSemantics.reason: send/recv needs a posted receive buffer and tag matching per message; slots are reserved per epoch instead

aiCoreRemoteAccess.reason: a remote load stalls the Core for at least one round trip (remoteLoadMinUs in the output); B=1 decode keeps it off the critical path

addressing.chosen: symmetric global address (rank, die, region, offset) with protection key and generation
alternatives: per-card physical addresses in every template
addressing.reason: templates store offsets only and stay card-independent
